gloss: when the time comes; when the opportunity arises

definitions.gloss: when the time comes; when the opportunity arises; at the right moment
definitions.explanation: An expression meaning to wait for an appropriate moment before taking action. Implies patience and timing rather than immediate action.

examples.japanese: {折|おり}を{見|み}て{相談|そうだん}します。
examples.english: I'll consult with you when the time is right.

examples.japanese: {折|おり}を{見|み}て{上司|じょうし}に{報告|ほうこく}しようと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I'm planning to report to my supervisor when the opportunity arises.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しそうだったので、{折|おり}を{見|み}て{声|こえ}をかけることにした。
examples.english: Since they looked busy, I decided to speak to them when the moment was right.

notes:
A set expression built on {折|おり} (occasion, opportunity) and {見|み}て (watching for). Expresses the idea of waiting for a suitable opening rather than acting immediately. Common in both business and everyday contexts.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {折|おり}を{見|み}て + verb: to do something when the time is right
- {折|おり}を{見|み}て{伝|つた}える: to tell someone when the opportunity arises
- {折|おり}を{見|み}て{訪|たず}ねる: to visit when the time comes

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {機会|きかい}を{見|み}て: when the opportunity comes — similar but slightly more formal
- {頃合|ころあ}いを{見|み}て: judging the right moment — emphasizes reading the situation
- タイミングを{見|み}て: watching for the right timing — more casual, uses loanword
- {折|おり}に{触|ふ}れて: from time to time; whenever the occasion arises — means repeatedly, not just once

REGISTER:
Polite and measured. Often used in workplace communication to signal that one will act thoughtfully rather than rushing.
